title: Web UI kanban: Done column shows no tasks despite 63 closed issues
description: The Done column in the web UI kanban board is empty even though there are 63 closed issues. The footer shows '63 closed' but none appear in the Done column. Need to investigate whether the API isn't returning closed issues or the frontend is filtering them out.
design:
## Summary

The Done column in the kanban board is empty despite 63 closed issues because the frontend's getKanbanIssues() function explicitly passes exclude_status='closed,tombstone' to the API, which filters out all closed issues server-side. The stats header correctly shows 63 closed (from the separate /api/stats endpoint), creating a confusing mismatch. The fix is to stop excluding closed issues from the kanban API call, but since the Done column could grow large, we should also add a sensible default limit with a Show all toggle.

## Technical Approach

The root cause is in internal/webui/frontend/src/api/issues.ts line 171, where getKanbanIssues() hardcodes exclude_status: 'closed,tombstone'. This was introduced in commit 92dec74 (Enhance /api/issues for Kanban) - the intent was likely a performance optimization, but it inadvertently hid all closed issues from the Done column.

Approach: Change the exclude_status to only exclude tombstone (not closed). Additionally, since the Done column could accumulate many closed issues over time, add a collapsed-by-default behavior to the Done column showing the most recent N closed issues with a Show all X button.

Trade-offs considered:
- Simplest fix: just remove closed from exclude_status. Pros: one-line change. Cons: Done column could be overwhelming with 63+ cards, degrading UX and performance.
- Chosen approach: Remove the exclusion AND add a default display limit of 10 in the Done column. This balances correctness with usability. The limit is purely frontend - the API returns all closed issues, and the column caps the display.

## Files to Modify

### 1. internal/webui/frontend/src/api/issues.ts (line 171)
Change: Update exclude_status from 'closed,tombstone' to 'tombstone'.
This is the root cause fix - closed issues will now be included in the kanban API response.
Update the JSDoc comment on line 166 to reflect the new behavior (Excludes tombstone issues).

### 2. internal/webui/frontend/src/components/KanbanBoard/KanbanBoard.tsx (around line 250-275)
Change: Add display-limiting logic for the Done column.
After grouping issues by column (line 164-181), for the done column specifically, sort by updated_at descending and cap at DONE_COLUMN_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 10.
Track a showAllDone boolean state. When true, show all issues; when false, show only the most recent 10.
Pass a footerAction prop to the Done column StatusColumn: Show all X closed button when truncated, Show recent when expanded.
This keeps the column manageable by default while allowing users to see everything.

### 3. internal/webui/frontend/src/components/KanbanBoard/columnConfigs.tsx
Change: Add an optional defaultLimit property to the done column config.
Add defaultLimit: 10 to the done column definition (line 94-101).
This makes the limit configurable through the column config rather than hardcoded in KanbanBoard.

### 4. internal/webui/frontend/src/components/KanbanBoard/types.ts
Change: Add defaultLimit?: number to the KanbanColumnConfig interface.
This optional field controls how many items to show by default before requiring Show all.

## Files to Create

None.

## Dependencies

No external packages needed.
No other tasks block this.

## Edge Cases and Error Handling

1. Zero closed issues: Done column should show empty state as before (EmptyColumn component already handles this).
2. Fewer than 10 closed issues: No Show all button needed; just display all of them.
3. Exactly 10 closed issues: No Show all button needed (limit is 10, showing 10 means showing all).
4. Drag to Done column: When a user drags a card to Done, the issue should appear in the column even if the limit is active. The onDragEnd callback already handles the status change; the issue will appear at the top of the Done column since it will have the most recent updated_at.
5. Drag from Done column: Should work normally - user should be able to drag from visible cards in Done back to other columns. Cards beyond the limit are simply not rendered and cannot be dragged.
6. Filter interactions: When filters are applied, the limit should apply after filtering. If a user searches and there are fewer than 10 matches in Done, no Show all button.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests
1. api/issues.ts: Update existing test for getKanbanIssues to verify the API is called with exclude_status=tombstone (not closed,tombstone).
2. KanbanBoard.test.tsx: Add test cases:
   - Done column shows closed issues (currently would fail - regression test).
   - Done column limits display to 10 items by default when more than 10 closed issues exist.
   - Show all button appears when Done column has more than 10 items.
   - Clicking Show all displays all closed issues.
   - Done column shows all items when 10 or fewer closed issues (no Show all button).
3. columnConfigs.test.ts: Verify the done column has defaultLimit: 10.

### Manual Verification
1. Open the kanban board with a project that has closed issues.
2. Verify the Done column shows the 10 most recently closed issues.
3. Verify a Show all X closed link appears at the bottom of the Done column.
4. Click Show all and verify all closed issues appear.
5. Drag a card to Done - verify it appears in the column.
6. Drag a card from Done back to another column - verify it moves correctly.
7. Verify the stats header count matches the total closed issues.
close_reason: Fixed Done column: changed exclude_status from closed,tombstone to tombstone, added defaultLimit:10 with Show all toggle

title: Remove dist/ from git and add to .gitignore
description: Remove committed frontend/dist/ from git tracking (git rm -r --cached) and add internal/webui/frontend/dist/ to .gitignore. This prevents stale UI artifacts in the repo and forces fresh frontend builds.
design:
## Summary

Remove the committed `internal/webui/frontend/dist/` directory from git tracking and add it to `.gitignore`. Currently, 12 build artifact files (~1.2MB) are tracked in git, causing stale UI artifacts to persist in the repo. After this change, `go:embed` will require a fresh `make frontend` build before `go build` can succeed, which is addressed by the dependent task loomcli-vw0.

## Technical Approach

This is a straightforward git hygiene task with two operations:
1. Remove `dist/` from git's index without deleting the local files (`git rm -r --cached`)
2. Add the path to `.gitignore` so it stays untracked

**Key consideration:** The `go:embed all:frontend/dist` directive in `internal/webui/embed.go` requires the `dist/` directory to exist at build time. After removing it from git, anyone cloning fresh will need to run `make frontend` before `go build`. This is intentional — the dependent task loomcli-vw0 will update the Makefile to enforce this dependency.

**Makefile comment update:** Line 45 of the Makefile has the comment "pre-built dist/ is committed for go build without Node.js" — this comment should be removed since it will no longer be true.

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `.gitignore`
Add `internal/webui/frontend/dist/` to the "Frontend" section (after the existing `node_modules/` entry on line 8):

```
# Frontend dependencies
internal/webui/frontend/node_modules/
internal/webui/frontend/dist/
```

### 2. `Makefile` (line 45)
Update the comment on the `frontend` target. Change:
```
# Run this after modifying frontend source; pre-built dist/ is committed for go build without Node.js
```
To:
```
# Run this after modifying frontend source; dist/ must exist for go:embed
```

## Git Operations

Run in this order:
1. `git rm -r --cached internal/webui/frontend/dist/` — removes 12 files from git index, keeps local copies
2. Edit `.gitignore` — add the ignore rule
3. Edit `Makefile` — update stale comment
4. Stage and commit all changes

## Dependencies

- **Blocks:** loomcli-vw0 (Make build/install depend on frontend build) — after dist/ is removed from git, the Makefile must be updated so `make build` and `make install` trigger `make frontend` first. That is a separate task.
- No external packages needed.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

- **Local dist/ preserved:** `git rm --cached` does NOT delete local files, so anyone with an existing checkout keeps their built dist/ and can still `go build` immediately.
- **Fresh clones break without `make frontend`:** This is expected and resolved by loomcli-vw0.
- **CI/CD:** If any CI pipeline runs `go build` without `make frontend`, it will fail. The Makefile dependency update (loomcli-vw0) must be merged together or immediately after this change.
- **Worktrees:** Other worktrees sharing the same repo will also see dist/ untracked after the commit propagates. They will need to run `make frontend` if their local dist/ is missing.

## Testing Strategy

1. After `git rm -r --cached`, verify: `git ls-files -- internal/webui/frontend/dist/` returns nothing (no tracked files)
2. Verify local files still exist: `ls internal/webui/frontend/dist/index.html` succeeds
3. Verify `.gitignore` works: `git status` should NOT show dist/ files as untracked
4. Verify `make frontend && go build ./...` still works (dist/ regenerated and embedded correctly)
close_reason: Removed dist/ from git tracking, added to .gitignore, updated Makefile comment

title: Create Backend interface and registry in backend.go
description: Create backend.go with: Backend interface (Name, InvokeInteractive, InvokeNonInteractive), backends map registry, activeBackend var (default claude), SetBackend/GetBackendName funcs. Move claudeInvoker/claudeNonInteractiveInvoker vars here rewired to dispatch through activeBackend. Move InvokeClaude/InvokeClaudeNonInteractive/InvokeClaudeForConflicts public API here.
design:
## Summary

Create `backend.go` in `internal/cli/` that introduces a `Backend` interface for abstracting AI coding agent invocations (currently hardcoded to Claude). This is the foundational piece for multi-CLI backend support (claude, codex, opencode). The file establishes the interface contract, a backend registry, and rewires the existing public API functions (`InvokeClaude`, `InvokeClaudeNonInteractive`, `InvokeClaudeForConflicts`) to dispatch through the active backend. All existing callers and tests continue to work with zero changes.

## Technical Approach

**Pattern**: Strategy pattern with a global registry and active backend selection. This matches the existing codebase pattern of using package-level vars with mockable function pointers (see `claudeInvoker`, `claudeNonInteractiveInvoker`, `execCommand`).

**Key design decisions**:
1. The `Backend` interface has 3 methods: `Name() string`, `InvokeInteractive(workDir, prompt, agentName string) error`, and `InvokeNonInteractive(workDir, prompt, agentName string, shutdown <-chan struct{}) error`.
2. A package-level `backends map[string]Backend` registry and `activeBackend` var (default "claude") provide the dispatch mechanism.
3. `RegisterBackend(b Backend)` adds to registry (called from `init()` in each backend file like `backend_claude.go`).
4. `SetBackend(name string) error` validates and switches the active backend.
5. `GetBackendName() string` returns the active backend name.
6. The existing public API functions (`InvokeClaude`, `InvokeClaudeNonInteractive`, `InvokeClaudeForConflicts`) remain in this file but are rewired to dispatch through the active backend. This preserves all call sites unchanged.
7. The existing mockable vars (`claudeInvoker`, `claudeNonInteractiveInvoker`) stay in `claude.go` for now — they will be moved in the follow-up task `loomcli-l8e` (Extract Claude backend). This task does NOT touch `claude.go`.

**Trade-off**: We considered moving the Claude implementation into `backend_claude.go` in this same task, but the downstream task `loomcli-l8e` is explicitly scoped for that extraction. Keeping this task focused on the interface + registry + dispatch means it's smaller and safer to review.

## Files to Create

### `internal/cli/backend.go`
The core file containing:
- `Backend` interface with 3 methods
- `backends` map registry (package-level, unexported)
- `activeBackend` string var (package-level, unexported, default "claude")
- `RegisterBackend(b Backend)` - adds backend to registry by `b.Name()`
- `SetBackend(name string) error` - validates name exists in registry, sets activeBackend
- `GetBackendName() string` - returns activeBackend string
- `ListBackends() []string` - returns sorted list of registered backend names (useful for help text/validation errors)
- Rewired public dispatch functions that delegate to the active backend:
  - `InvokeBackend(workDir, prompt, agentName string) error` - dispatches to `activeBackend.InvokeInteractive()`
  - `InvokeBackendNonInteractive(workDir, prompt, agentName string, shutdown <-chan struct{}) error` - dispatches to `activeBackend.InvokeNonInteractive()`
- NOTE: The existing `InvokeClaude`, `InvokeClaudeNonInteractive`, `InvokeClaudeForConflicts` functions stay in `claude.go` unchanged. They are NOT moved or rewired in this task. The rewiring happens later when callers are updated to use `InvokeBackend` / `InvokeBackendNonInteractive`.

### `internal/cli/backend_test.go`
Tests for:
- `RegisterBackend` adds to registry correctly
- `RegisterBackend` with duplicate name overwrites (no error, last-wins)
- `SetBackend` with valid name succeeds
- `SetBackend` with invalid name returns error listing available backends
- `GetBackendName` returns default "claude"
- `GetBackendName` returns updated name after `SetBackend`
- `ListBackends` returns sorted names
- `InvokeBackend` dispatches to active backend's `InvokeInteractive`
- `InvokeBackendNonInteractive` dispatches to active backend's `InvokeNonInteractive`
- `InvokeBackend` with unregistered active backend returns error (defensive)
- Mock backend struct implementing the interface for test use

## Files to Modify

None. This task creates new files only. Existing `claude.go` is untouched — the Claude implementation stays as-is and will be extracted into `backend_claude.go` in `loomcli-l8e`.

## Dependencies

- No external packages needed — only stdlib (`fmt`, `sort`, `sync`)
- No internal module dependencies beyond being in the `cli` package
- No tasks need to be completed first (this IS the first task in the dependency chain)

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **SetBackend with unknown name**: Return descriptive error: `fmt.Errorf("unknown backend %q; available: %v", name, ListBackends())`
2. **InvokeBackend when activeBackend not in registry**: Return error `fmt.Errorf("backend %q not registered", activeBackend)`. This can happen if `SetBackend` is bypassed or if the Claude backend init hasn't run.
3. **Concurrent access**: Use `sync.RWMutex` to protect `backends` map and `activeBackend` var, since `RegisterBackend` is called from `init()` (sequential) but `SetBackend`/`GetBackendName` could theoretically be called concurrently. Lightweight protection.
4. **Empty registry**: `ListBackends` returns empty slice; `InvokeBackend` returns error.
5. **RegisterBackend with nil**: Panic (programming error, not runtime).

## Testing Strategy

### Unit tests (`backend_test.go`):
- Create a `mockBackend` struct implementing `Backend` that records calls
- Test registry operations (register, set, get, list)
- Test dispatch functions route to the correct backend
- Test error cases (unknown backend, unregistered active backend)
- Test concurrent safety with multiple goroutines calling SetBackend/GetBackendName

### Manual verification:
- Run `go build ./...` to verify compilation
- Run `go test ./internal/cli/...` to verify all existing tests still pass (no changes to claude.go means no breakage)
- Run `go vet ./internal/cli/` for correctness
close_reason: Completed: Backend interface, registry, dispatch functions with full test coverage including concurrency tests

title: Create e2e Dockerfile with Go + Node.js + all backend CLIs
design:
## Summary

This task creates a multi-stage Dockerfile for running loomcli E2E tests in an isolated container environment. The container includes Go (for building loom and running go test with -tags e2e), Node.js (for Playwright frontend tests), tmux (for automode tests), git, the bd CLI, and stub scripts for all three backend CLIs (claude, codex, opencode). The Dockerfile lives at e2e/Dockerfile and is designed to be built and invoked by the sibling tasks (run_local.sh, run_test.sh, container_test.go).

## Technical Approach

**Strategy: Multi-stage build with stub backends**

Stage 1 (builder): Compile Go binaries (loom, logrouter) and install Go test dependencies. This uses the official Go image and produces static binaries.

Stage 2 (frontend): Install Node.js dependencies and build the frontend (for Playwright tests). This uses an official Node.js image.

Stage 3 (runtime): Based on a Debian slim image, this stage includes:
- Go toolchain (needed for `go test -tags e2e` at runtime)
- Node.js + npm (needed for Playwright browser tests)
- tmux, git, jq, curl (system utilities for e2e tests)
- The compiled loom and logrouter binaries from stage 1
- The full source tree (needed for `go test`)
- Stub scripts for claude/codex/opencode in /usr/local/bin
- The bd CLI (built from third_party/beads or downloaded)
- The frontend build output from stage 2

**Key design decisions:**

1. **Stubs over real CLIs**: Backend CLIs (claude, codex, opencode) are replaced with configurable stub scripts that mimic expected output formats. For claude: outputs stream-json events. For codex: outputs plain text. For opencode: outputs plain text. This allows full-path E2E testing without real API keys. Real CLIs can be mounted at runtime via volume mounts to /usr/local/bin/ if needed.

2. **Go toolchain in runtime image**: Unlike a typical production Dockerfile that only copies binaries, we keep the Go toolchain because E2E tests are executed with `go test -tags e2e ./internal/cli/...` which requires compilation.

3. **Single runtime base**: Use golang:1.25-bookworm as the runtime base (not alpine) because:
   - tmux and PTY tests need glibc
   - Playwright browsers need Debian-based libraries
   - Go toolchain is needed anyway, so no size penalty
   - Avoids CGO/musl issues

4. **bd CLI**: Built from the vendored third_party/beads source during the build stage, since bd is a Go binary in the same module tree. If that doesn't work, the bd binary can be downloaded from a release.

5. **Entrypoint**: The default CMD runs `go test -tags e2e -v ./...` but can be overridden to run specific test suites or the smoke test.

**Trade-offs:**
- Image size (~1.5-2GB) is large due to Go toolchain + Node.js + Playwright browsers, but E2E test images aren't meant for production deployment
- Stubs are simpler than mocking at the Go level but less precise; this is intentional since the stubs test the full command invocation path
- Frontend dist/ is committed, so the Node.js stage could be skipped, but including it ensures tests run against a fresh build

## Files to Create

### 1. `e2e/Dockerfile`
The main multi-stage Dockerfile. Approximately 120-150 lines.

**Stage 1: builder** (golang:1.25-bookworm)
- COPY go.mod, go.sum; run go mod download
- COPY full source tree
- RUN go build -o /out/loom ./cmd/loom
- RUN go build -o /out/logrouter ./cmd/logrouter
- Build bd CLI if it has a main.go in third_party/beads

**Stage 2: frontend** (node:20-bookworm-slim)
- WORKDIR /app/internal/webui/frontend
- COPY internal/webui/frontend/package*.json .
- RUN npm ci
- COPY internal/webui/frontend/ .
- RUN npm run build

**Stage 3: runtime** (golang:1.25-bookworm)
- Install system packages: tmux, git, jq, curl, ca-certificates
- Install Node.js 20 via nodesource or copy from node image
- Install Playwright and browsers (npx playwright install --with-deps chromium)
- COPY compiled binaries from builder stage
- COPY full source tree (for go test)
- COPY frontend build from frontend stage over dist/
- COPY stub scripts to /usr/local/bin/
- Set up working directory and environment
- ENV LOOM_BACKEND=claude TERM=xterm-256color
- ENTRYPOINT allows override; CMD defaults to running e2e tests

### 2. `e2e/stubs/claude`
Stub script (~40 lines) that mimics the Claude CLI:
- When invoked as `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions <prompt>`: outputs simulated interactive session, exits 0
- When invoked as `claude -p --verbose --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions`: reads prompt from stdin, outputs valid stream-json events (assistant message with text content block, then result event), exits 0
- Configurable via STUB_CLAUDE_EXIT_CODE env var for testing error paths
- Configurable via STUB_CLAUDE_RESPONSE env var for custom response text
- Configurable via STUB_CLAUDE_DELAY env var for simulating latency

### 3. `e2e/stubs/codex`
Stub script (~30 lines) that mimics the Codex CLI:
- When invoked as `codex --full-auto <prompt>`: outputs simulated response, exits 0
- When invoked as `codex exec --json`: reads prompt from stdin, outputs JSON response, exits 0
- Configurable via STUB_CODEX_EXIT_CODE, STUB_CODEX_RESPONSE, STUB_CODEX_DELAY

### 4. `e2e/stubs/opencode`
Stub script (~30 lines) that mimics the OpenCode CLI:
- When invoked as `opencode --prompt <prompt>`: outputs simulated response, exits 0
- When invoked as `opencode run --format json`: reads prompt from stdin, outputs JSON response, exits 0
- Configurable via STUB_OPENCODE_EXIT_CODE, STUB_OPENCODE_RESPONSE, STUB_OPENCODE_DELAY

### 5. `e2e/.dockerignore`
Prevents copying unnecessary files into the build context:
- .git/ (large, not needed inside container since tests create their own repos)
- worktrees/ (agent worktrees, not relevant)
- .beads/ (issue tracker data, not needed for tests)
- node_modules/ (will be installed fresh)
- *.log

### 6. `e2e/README.md`
Brief usage documentation explaining:
- How to build: `docker build -f e2e/Dockerfile -t loomcli-e2e .`
- How to run all e2e tests: `docker run loomcli-e2e`
- How to run specific tests: `docker run loomcli-e2e go test -tags e2e -v -run TestE2E_TmuxSessionLifecycle ./internal/cli/`
- How to mount real backend CLIs: `docker run -v $(which claude):/usr/local/bin/claude loomcli-e2e`
- How to pass API keys: `docker run -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... loomcli-e2e`
- Environment variable reference for stub configuration

## Files to Modify

None. This is a pure additive task creating new files in the e2e/ directory.

## Dependencies

- **External packages**: None beyond what's in go.mod
- **System packages installed in Dockerfile**: tmux, git, jq, curl, ca-certificates, Node.js 20, Playwright + Chromium
- **Base images**: golang:1.25-bookworm, node:20-bookworm-slim
- **Internal**: Uses the existing go.mod, the full source tree, and the frontend build system
- **No blocking tasks**: This task depends only on the epic (grouping), no other implementation tasks

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Go 1.25 image availability**: go.mod specifies 1.25.6. If golang:1.25-bookworm doesn't exist yet, use golang:1.24-bookworm and accept minor version mismatch, or use golang:latest with a version check. Add an ARG GO_VERSION=1.25 to make it configurable.

2. **bd CLI build**: The bd binary may live in third_party/beads as a Go binary (cmd/bd/main.go). If that path doesn't exist or build fails, the Dockerfile should fall back to downloading a release from GitHub. Use a conditional RUN step.

3. **Playwright browser install failures**: Playwright browser downloads can be flaky. Use `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` (just Chromium, not all browsers) to minimize download size and failure surface. Cache the browser install in a Docker layer.

4. **Stub script robustness**: Stubs should handle both interactive and non-interactive invocation patterns. They should write to both stdout and stderr as appropriate. They should respect the shutdown signal (SIGTERM) and exit cleanly.

5. **tmux in container**: tmux requires a proper terminal. The e2e tests use detached sessions (`tmux new-session -d`) which work without a TTY. The Dockerfile sets TERM=xterm-256color to ensure tmux is happy.

6. **Build context size**: The .dockerignore must exclude .git/ and worktrees/ to keep the build context manageable. The full source tree is ~50MB without these.

7. **Cached layers**: Order Dockerfile instructions for maximum cache reuse: system packages first (rarely change), then go.mod/go.sum (change occasionally), then source code (changes frequently).

## Testing Strategy

### Build verification:
1. `docker build -f e2e/Dockerfile -t loomcli-e2e .` should complete without errors
2. Verify all binaries exist: `docker run loomcli-e2e which loom logrouter claude codex opencode bd git tmux`
3. Verify Go version: `docker run loomcli-e2e go version`
4. Verify Node version: `docker run loomcli-e2e node --version`

### Stub verification:
1. `docker run loomcli-e2e claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "test"` should output simulated response and exit 0
2. `docker run loomcli-e2e sh -c 'echo test | claude -p --verbose --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions'` should output valid stream-json
3. Same for codex and opencode stubs
4. `docker run -e STUB_CLAUDE_EXIT_CODE=1 loomcli-e2e claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "test"` should exit 1

### E2E test execution:
1. `docker run loomcli-e2e go test -tags e2e -v -run TestE2E_TmuxSession ./internal/cli/` should pass
2. All existing e2e tests should pass inside the container

### Integration with sibling tasks:
- The container_test.go harness (loomcli-rn0) will build this image and run tests programmatically
- run_local.sh (loomcli-00s) will use `docker run` with volume mounts
- verify_todo.sh (loomcli-d9c) will be the smoke test entrypoint
- run_test.sh (loomcli-uqa) will orchestrate test suites

title: E2E stub scripts: JSON injection when RESPONSE contains quotes
description: E2E stub scripts (claude, codex, opencode) use printf to interpolate STUB_*_RESPONSE into JSON without escaping. Quotes or backslashes in the response break the JSON output. Fix: use jq -Rs to escape the value, or document the limitation.
design:
## Summary

The E2E stub scripts (claude, codex, opencode) use `printf` to interpolate `STUB_*_RESPONSE` directly into JSON strings. If the response contains double quotes, backslashes, newlines, or other JSON-special characters, the output becomes invalid JSON. Instead of adding an escape helper function (previous design), this revision uses `jq -n --arg` to construct entire JSON objects, eliminating string interpolation for JSON values entirely.

## Technical Approach

Replace each `printf` that interpolates a response into JSON with a `jq -n --arg` call that constructs the complete JSON object. `jq --arg name value` binds a shell variable as a properly-escaped JSON string that can be referenced as `$name` in the jq filter. This is the idiomatic way to build JSON from shell variables — no escaping logic, no helper functions, no fallbacks.

**Why this approach over the previous design:**
- **No code duplication**: The previous design copied a `json_escape` function into all 3 stubs. This approach needs zero shared code.
- **No escape logic at all**: `jq --arg` handles escaping internally. There is no `json_escape` function to get wrong.
- **No fallback needed**: jq is installed in the Dockerfile (line 39). The stubs only run inside the container. If jq is somehow missing, the script should fail loudly rather than silently produce broken JSON.
- **Simpler diff**: Each fix is a single-line replacement.

## Files to Create

None.

## Files to Modify

### e2e/stubs/claude

Replace line 47:
```sh
# Before:
printf '{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"%s"}]}}\n' "$RESPONSE"

# After:
jq -nc --arg t "$RESPONSE" '{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":$t}]}}'
```

The `jq -n` flag means "null input" (no stdin needed). The `-c` flag produces compact single-line output. `--arg t "$RESPONSE"` binds the shell variable as a JSON string accessible as `$t` in the filter. The `$t` reference inside the jq expression (without quotes) tells jq to insert the properly-escaped string value.

Line 48 (`printf` for the result event) has no variable interpolation and remains unchanged.

### e2e/stubs/codex

Replace line 41:
```sh
# Before:
printf '{"status":"completed","output":"%s"}\n' "$RESPONSE"

# After:
jq -nc --arg o "$RESPONSE" '{"status":"completed","output":$o}'
```

### e2e/stubs/opencode

Replace line 44:
```sh
# Before:
printf '{"status":"completed","output":"%s"}\n' "$RESPONSE"

# After:
jq -nc --arg o "$RESPONSE" '{"status":"completed","output":$o}'
```

## Dependencies

- `jq` must be installed in the runtime environment (already present — Dockerfile line 39)
- No new dependencies

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Empty response**: `jq --arg t ""` produces `""` — valid empty JSON string. Verified behavior.
2. **Response with double quotes**: `jq --arg` escapes to `\"` automatically.
3. **Response with newlines**: Escaped to `\n` in the JSON string value.
4. **Response with backslashes**: Escaped to `\\`.
5. **Response with Unicode**: jq handles Unicode correctly.
6. **jq not available**: The script will fail with "command not found". This is correct behavior — a silent fallback that produces broken JSON is worse than a clear failure. jq is guaranteed by the Dockerfile.
7. **Non-JSON paths unaffected**: The `echo "$RESPONSE"` calls in interactive/fallback paths output plain text, not JSON. No changes needed there.

## Testing Strategy

1. **Manual test with quotes**: Set `STUB_CLAUDE_RESPONSE=He said hello` and verify `jq .` can parse the output.
2. **Manual test with backslashes**: Set `STUB_CODEX_RESPONSE=path\to\file` and verify valid JSON.
3. **Manual test with newlines**: Set `STUB_OPENCODE_RESPONSE` to a multi-line value and verify JSON contains `\n` escapes.
4. **Regression test**: Run stubs with default responses and verify output is byte-identical (jq -nc output matches the previous printf output for simple strings with no special chars).
5. **shellcheck**: Run `shellcheck e2e/stubs/claude e2e/stubs/codex e2e/stubs/opencode` to verify no issues.
6. **Docker build + test**: `docker build -f e2e/Dockerfile -t loomcli-e2e . && docker run loomcli-e2e` to verify all E2E tests still pass.
close_reason: Fixed JSON injection in all 3 E2E stubs by replacing printf with jq -nc --arg. Manually tested with quotes, backslashes, newlines, empty, and default responses.

title: Fix doctor_test.go beadsDirOnce.Do(func(){}) no-op pattern
description: In doctor_test.go, 5 test cases do ResetBeadsDirCache(); beadsDirCache = dir; beadsDirOnce.Do(func(){}) but the empty Do() just wastes the once slot. The next real GetBeadsDir() call re-runs initialization and overwrites the test dir. Fix by using t.Setenv or calling GetBeadsDir() after setting env vars. Lines 201, 221, 246, 353, 369.
design:
## Summary

Five test cases in doctor_test.go use the pattern `ResetBeadsDirCache(); beadsDirCache = dir; beadsDirOnce.Do(func(){})` to force `GetBeadsDir()` to return a specific directory. While this pattern works, it directly manipulates package internals (`beadsDirCache` and `beadsDirOnce`) instead of using the public API. The fix replaces this fragile pattern with proper test setup: writing a workspace config via `setupWorkspaceConfig()` so that `GetBeadsDir()` returns the desired directory through normal initialization, matching the pattern already used in `worktree_beadsdir_test.go`.

## Technical Approach

The codebase already has a test helper `setupWorkspaceConfig(t, cfg)` in `worktree_workspace_test.go` that:
1. Creates a temp config dir
2. Sets `LOOM_CONFIG_DIR` via `t.Setenv`
3. Writes a valid `config.yaml` with workspace config

By calling `ResetBeadsDirCache()` and then `setupWorkspaceConfig()` with a workspace whose `Path` equals the test's temp dir, `GetBeadsDir()` will naturally return that dir through its normal code path (LoadConfig → find workspace → return workspace path). This eliminates direct manipulation of `beadsDirCache` and `beadsDirOnce`.

Key design decision: Use the existing `setupWorkspaceConfig` helper rather than introducing a new test helper. This keeps the approach consistent with `worktree_beadsdir_test.go`.

## Files to Modify

### `internal/cli/doctor_test.go`
Five locations need the same transformation:

**Lines 199-201 (TestCheckProjectConfig / "no loom.yaml")**:
- Remove: `beadsDirCache = dir` and `beadsDirOnce.Do(func() {})`
- Already has `ResetBeadsDirCache()` and `t.Setenv("LOOM_CONFIG_DIR", dir)` — but need to set up workspace config so `GetBeadsDir()` returns `dir`
- Add: call `setupWorkspaceConfig(t, &LoomConfig{DefaultWorkspace: "test", Workspaces: map[string]WorkspaceConfig{"test": {Path: dir}}})` after `ResetBeadsDirCache()`
- Remove the existing `t.Setenv("LOOM_CONFIG_DIR", dir)` since `setupWorkspaceConfig` sets it
- Note: This test needs `loom.yaml` to NOT exist in `dir`. Since `setupWorkspaceConfig` writes `config.yaml` (global config) to a *separate* temp dir and only sets `LOOM_CONFIG_DIR` to that config dir, the workspace path (our `dir`) won't have `loom.yaml` — test still works correctly.

**Lines 219-221 (TestCheckProjectConfig / "invalid loom.yaml")**:
- Same transformation as above
- Remove: `beadsDirCache = dir` and `beadsDirOnce.Do(func() {})`
- The test writes an invalid `loom.yaml` to `dir` — this still works because `checkProjectConfig` calls `GetBeadsDir()` then looks for `loom.yaml` in that dir
- Replace `t.Setenv("LOOM_CONFIG_DIR", dir)` and manual cache manipulation with `setupWorkspaceConfig`

**Lines 244-246 (TestCheckProjectConfig / "valid loom.yaml")**:
- Same transformation
- Remove: `beadsDirCache = dir` and `beadsDirOnce.Do(func() {})`
- Replace with `setupWorkspaceConfig`

**Lines 351-353 (TestCheckBeadsInit / "beads initialized")**:
- Remove: `beadsDirCache = dir` and `beadsDirOnce.Do(func() {})`
- Add: `setupWorkspaceConfig(t, &LoomConfig{DefaultWorkspace: "test", Workspaces: map[string]WorkspaceConfig{"test": {Path: dir}}})`
- Keep `ResetBeadsDirCache()` (it's needed before `setupWorkspaceConfig`)

**Lines 367-369 (TestCheckBeadsInit / "beads not initialized")**:
- Same transformation as above

For the TestCheckBeadsInit tests, the `defer ResetBeadsDirCache()` can be removed since `setupWorkspaceConfig` uses `t.Setenv` which is automatically cleaned up, and each test already calls `ResetBeadsDirCache()` at the start. Actually, keep the `defer ResetBeadsDirCache()` for safety — it ensures other tests in the same package aren't affected by stale cache.

## Dependencies

- No external packages needed
- Uses existing `setupWorkspaceConfig` helper from `worktree_workspace_test.go` (same package, so accessible)
- Uses existing types `LoomConfig`, `WorkspaceConfig`

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

- `setupWorkspaceConfig` creates its own temp dir for the config, separate from the test's temp dir used for test data (loom.yaml, .beads/). This is correct behavior — the global config dir and workspace dir should be separate.
- Some TestCheckProjectConfig tests also pass `LOOM_CONFIG_DIR` — but `setupWorkspaceConfig` overwrites it, which is fine since the workspace path (not the config dir) is what matters for `GetBeadsDir()`.
- ResetBeadsDirCache must be called before setupWorkspaceConfig to ensure a fresh sync.Once.

## Testing Strategy

- Run `go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestCheckProjectConfig` to verify all 3 sub-tests pass
- Run `go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestCheckBeadsInit` to verify both sub-tests pass
- Run `go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestDoctor` to verify no regressions in other doctor tests
- Run the full test suite: `go test ./internal/cli/...`
- Verify that no test file directly references `beadsDirCache` or `beadsDirOnce` anymore (only `worktree.go` and `ResetBeadsDirCache()` should reference them)

title: Daemon: skip WIP commit on startup when worktree is clean
description: In daemon.go, the startup reset creates a WIP commit even when the worktree is clean (IsCleanWorkingTree returns true). The commit guard on line 159-164 checks for dirty state, but the branch checkout still happens and a commit was already made. Move the clean check to also gate the WIP commit message — only commit if actually dirty. Currently produces empty 'WIP: daemon startup reset from X' commits that pollute git history.
design:
## Summary

The daemon startup reset in `resetWorktreeBranches()` can create empty WIP commits when the worktree is clean. The root cause is twofold: (1) `IsCleanWorkingTree` errors are silently discarded with `_`, causing the error case (`clean=false`) to incorrectly trigger a WIP commit attempt, and (2) `commitWIP()` itself has no safety check — it blindly runs `git add -A; git commit -m` without verifying there are actually staged changes. This fix makes both layers defensive against empty commits.

## Technical Approach

Two-layer defense:

1. **Handle `IsCleanWorkingTree` errors properly in `resetWorktreeBranches`** — if the check fails, log the error and skip the WIP commit (erring on the side of not creating spurious commits). The checkout still proceeds; worst case, checkout fails on a dirty tree and the warning is logged.

2. **Make `commitWIP` defensive** — after `git add -A`, check if there are actually staged changes using `git diff --cached --quiet`. If exit code is 0 (nothing staged), return nil without committing. This protects all callers of `commitWIP` (both `resetWorktreeBranches` and `EnsureWorktreeBranch`) from creating empty commits.

Trade-off: We could also use `git commit --allow-empty` to make it never fail, but that would be the opposite of what we want — we want to *prevent* empty commits, not allow them.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/cli/daemon.go` (lines 159-165)

In `resetWorktreeBranches()`, change:
```go
clean, _ := IsCleanWorkingTree(ap.worktreePath)
if !clean {
```
to:
```go
clean, cleanErr := IsCleanWorkingTree(ap.worktreePath)
if cleanErr != nil {
    log.Printf("[daemon] Warning: failed to check worktree cleanliness for %s: %v", ap.entry.Worktree, cleanErr)
    // Skip WIP commit on error — checkout may fail below, which is logged separately
} else if !clean {
```

This ensures that when `IsCleanWorkingTree` errors, we don't treat it as dirty and create a spurious WIP commit.

### 2. `internal/cli/daemon_branch.go` (commitWIP function, lines 77-85)

After `git add -A`, add a staged-changes check before committing:
```go
func commitWIP(worktreePath, message string) error {
    if _, err := RunGitCommand(worktreePath, "add", "-A"); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("git add failed: %w", err)
    }
    // Check if anything was actually staged
    if _, err := RunGitCommand(worktreePath, "diff", "--cached", "--quiet"); err == nil {
        // Exit code 0 means no staged changes — nothing to commit
        return nil
    }
    if _, err := RunGitCommand(worktreePath, "commit", "-m", message); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("git commit failed: %w", err)
    }
    return nil
}
```

`git diff --cached --quiet` exits 0 if the index matches HEAD (nothing staged), and exits 1 if there are differences. So `err == nil` means nothing to commit.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **`IsCleanWorkingTree` returns error**: Now logs a warning and skips WIP commit instead of treating as dirty.
2. **`git add -A` stages nothing**: `git diff --cached --quiet` returns 0, so `commitWIP` returns nil without attempting `git commit`.
3. **`git diff --cached --quiet` itself errors**: Treated as "there are changes" (err != nil), so we fall through to `git commit`. This is the safe default — worst case we attempt a commit that might fail.
4. **`EnsureWorktreeBranch` callers**: Also benefit from the `commitWIP` fix since they call the same function.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests to Add/Modify

1. **`daemon_branch_test.go`**: Add test `TestCommitWIP_NothingToCommit`:
   - Mock `git add -A` success, `git diff --cached --quiet` success (exit 0)
   - Assert `commitWIP` returns nil without calling `git commit`

2. **`daemon_branch_test.go`**: Add test `TestCommitWIP_WithStagedChanges`:
   - Mock `git add -A` success, `git diff --cached --quiet` failure (exit 1), `git commit` success
   - Assert `commitWIP` returns nil and commit was called

3. **Existing `TestCommitWIP` tests**: Update the "success" test case to include the `git diff --cached --quiet` mock (exits 1, meaning there ARE staged changes).

### Manual Verification

1. Set up a daemon with multiple worktrees
2. Ensure all worktrees are clean
3. Start the daemon and check git log — no empty WIP commits should be created
4. Introduce dirty changes in one worktree, restart daemon — only the dirty worktree should get a WIP commit

design:
## Summary

Create `internal/cli/config.go` with Go struct types representing the loom configuration hierarchy (`LoomConfig`, `RepoConfig`, `WorkspaceConfig`) and a `LoadConfig()` function that reads and parses `~/.loom/config.yaml`. This is the foundational building block for multi-repo workspace support — all downstream tasks (T2-T12) depend on these types and the loader. The implementation must be backwards compatible: when no config file exists, `LoadConfig()` returns nil (not an error), preserving existing single-repo behavior.

## Technical Approach

**Architecture**: A single `config.go` file containing struct definitions and loading functions. No global config singleton — callers receive a `*LoomConfig` and pass it explicitly. This follows the codebase's existing pattern of explicit dependency passing (e.g., `worktreePath` passed to lock functions).

**YAML parsing**: Use `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` — the standard Go YAML library. It's mature, well-maintained, and the task description explicitly requires it.

**Design decisions**:
- `LoadConfig()` returns `(*LoomConfig, error)` — nil config means no file found (not an error). Malformed YAML is an error.
- Helper functions (`GetConfigDir()`, `GetWorkspaceDir()`, `IsWorkspaceMode()`) are package-level free functions, consistent with existing patterns like `GetWorktreesDir()` and `GetDefaultBranch()`.
- Config dir defaults to `~/.loom/` but can be overridden via `LOOM_CONFIG_DIR` env var (follows the existing env-var override pattern).

## Files to Create

### 1. `internal/cli/config.go`
Core config types and loader. Contains:

```go
// LoomConfig is the top-level configuration from ~/.loom/config.yaml
type LoomConfig struct {
    DefaultWorkspace string            `yaml:"default_workspace,omitempty"`
    Workspaces       map[string]WorkspaceConfig `yaml:"workspaces"`
}

// WorkspaceConfig defines a named workspace containing multiple repos
type WorkspaceConfig struct {
    Path  string       `yaml:"path"`            // Directory path for this workspace
    Repos []RepoConfig `yaml:"repos"`           // Repositories in this workspace
}

// RepoConfig defines a single repository within a workspace
type RepoConfig struct {
    Name          string `yaml:"name"`                      // Display name / identifier
    Path          string `yaml:"path"`                      // Path to the repo (absolute or relative to workspace)
    DefaultBranch string `yaml:"default_branch,omitempty"`  // Override default branch (defaults to "main")
    Remote        string `yaml:"remote,omitempty"`          // Git remote name (defaults to "origin")
}
```

Functions:
- `GetConfigDir() string` — Returns `~/.loom`, respects `LOOM_CONFIG_DIR` env var. Panics/returns empty on `os.UserHomeDir()` failure (matches Go convention for home dir).
- `GetConfigPath() string` — Returns `GetConfigDir() + "/config.yaml"`.
- `LoadConfig() (*LoomConfig, error)` — Reads and parses the config file. Returns `(nil, nil)` if file doesn't exist. Returns `(nil, err)` on read/parse errors.
- `GetWorkspaceDir(name string) string` — Returns `GetConfigDir() + "/workspaces/" + name`. Pure path computation, no I/O.
- `IsWorkspaceMode() bool` — Returns true if config file exists AND has at least one workspace defined. Calls `LoadConfig()` internally.

### 2. `internal/cli/config_test.go`
Comprehensive tests. Contains:

- `TestGetConfigDir` — Default (`~/.loom`) and env var override (`LOOM_CONFIG_DIR`).
- `TestGetConfigPath` — Verifies path ends with `/config.yaml`.
- `TestLoadConfigMissing` — No config file → returns `(nil, nil)`.
- `TestLoadConfigValid` — Write a valid YAML file to temp dir, load it, verify all fields.
- `TestLoadConfigInvalidYAML` — Write malformed YAML → returns error.
- `TestLoadConfigEmptyFile` — Empty file → returns `(*LoomConfig{}, nil)` (valid but empty).
- `TestGetWorkspaceDir` — Verifies path construction.
- `TestIsWorkspaceMode` — True when config has workspaces, false when missing or empty.
- `TestRepoConfigDefaults` — Verify omitempty fields work correctly.

Test pattern: Use `t.TempDir()` for temp directories, `os.Setenv`/`defer os.Unsetenv` for env overrides (matching `worktree_test.go` patterns).

## Files to Modify

### 1. `go.mod`
Add dependency: `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`. Run `go get gopkg.in/yaml.v3` which will update both `go.mod` and `go.sum`.

## Dependencies

- **External**: `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` — YAML parsing library
- **Internal**: `os`, `path/filepath`, `fmt` — standard library only
- **No dependency on other loom packages** — this is a leaf dependency

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **No config file**: `LoadConfig()` returns `(nil, nil)`. This is the backwards-compatible default. Callers check `if cfg == nil { /* legacy single-repo mode */ }`.
2. **Config file exists but is empty**: Returns a zero-value `*LoomConfig` (not nil). `IsWorkspaceMode()` returns false.
3. **Malformed YAML**: Returns `(nil, error)` with descriptive message including the file path.
4. **Permission denied on config file**: Returns `(nil, error)` — standard os error wrapping.
5. **Home directory unavailable**: `GetConfigDir()` returns empty string, `LoadConfig()` will fail gracefully.
6. **`LOOM_CONFIG_DIR` override**: Allows testing and non-standard installations.
7. **Workspace with no repos**: Valid config, `IsWorkspaceMode()` returns true (workspace exists even if empty — repos may be added later via `loom config add-repo`).

## Testing Strategy

**Unit tests** (in `config_test.go`):
- Table-driven tests for `GetConfigDir` with/without env var
- File-based tests: write YAML to temp dir, set `LOOM_CONFIG_DIR`, call `LoadConfig()`
- Error cases: invalid YAML, missing file, empty file
- `IsWorkspaceMode()` integration: test with real temp config files

**Manual verification**:
1. `go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestConfig -v` — all config tests pass
2. `go test ./internal/cli/ -v` — all existing tests still pass (no regressions)
3. `go vet ./...` — no warnings
4. Create a sample `~/.loom/config.yaml` and verify `LoadConfig()` parses it correctly

**Sample config.yaml for testing**:
```yaml
default_workspace: myproject
workspaces:
  myproject:
    path: ~/.loom/workspaces/myproject
    repos:
      - name: backend
        path: /home/user/repos/backend
        default_branch: main
      - name: frontend
        path: /home/user/repos/frontend
        default_branch: develop
        remote: upstream
```
close_reason: Implemented config.go with LoomConfig/WorkspaceConfig/RepoConfig types, LoadConfig(), GetConfigDir(), GetConfigPath(), GetWorkspaceDir(), IsWorkspaceMode(). Added yaml.v3 dependency. All 9 tests passing.

title: Fix prompt exposure in ExternalBackend.InvokeInteractive
description: InvokeInteractive in backend_external.go:28 passes the prompt as a positional CLI arg (exec.Command(binPath, "invoke", "--interactive", prompt)), making it visible via ps aux. The non-interactive path correctly uses stdin pipe. Should pass prompt via stdin consistently. From PR #11 review.
design:
## Summary

ExternalBackend.InvokeInteractive passes the prompt as a positional CLI argument (`exec.Command(binPath, \"invoke\", \"--interactive\", prompt)`), making it visible to all users on the system via `ps aux`. This is a security issue — prompts may contain task descriptions, code snippets, or system instructions with sensitive data. The non-interactive path already correctly uses stdin pipe. This fix makes the interactive path use stdin consistently.

## Technical Approach

**Approach: Pass prompt via stdin using `io.MultiReader`**

Remove the prompt from CLI args and pipe it via stdin, followed by os.Stdin for interactive terminal input:

1. Create an `os.Pipe()` and write the prompt to it (same pattern as `InvokeNonInteractive`)
2. Close the write end of the pipe after writing the prompt
3. Use `io.MultiReader(pipeReader, os.Stdin)` as `cmd.Stdin`
4. When the external backend reads stdin, it gets the prompt first (terminated by EOF on the pipe), then seamlessly reads from `os.Stdin` for interactive input

**TTY consideration:** Since `cmd.Stdin` is an `io.Reader` (not an `*os.File`), Go will create an internal pipe. The child process's fd 0 will be a pipe, not a TTY. This means `isatty(0)` returns false. However:
- The external backend already knows it's in interactive mode via the `--interactive` flag — it should use that flag, not `isatty()`, to determine mode
- If the backend needs raw terminal access, it can open `/dev/tty` directly (standard Unix pattern)
- This matches how the non-interactive path already works — stdin is a pipe in both cases now

**Why not environment variable?** While `LOOM_PROMPT` env var would preserve the TTY on stdin, env vars are also visible via `/proc/<pid>/environ` (Linux) or `ps eww` (macOS). The stdin approach is more secure and consistent with the non-interactive path, as the task description requests.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/cli/backend_external.go`

**Change `InvokeInteractive` method (lines 27-39):**

Current:
```go
func (e *ExternalBackend) InvokeInteractive(workDir, prompt, agentName string) error {
    cmd := exec.Command(e.binPath, "invoke", "--interactive", prompt)
    cmd.Dir = workDir
    env := append(FilteredEnv(), "LOOM_WORKTREE_PATH="+workDir)
    if agentName != "" {
        env = append(env, "BD_ACTOR="+agentName)
    }
    cmd.Env = env
    cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
    cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
    cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
    return cmd.Run()
}
```

New:
```go
func (e *ExternalBackend) InvokeInteractive(workDir, prompt, agentName string) error {
    cmd := exec.Command(e.binPath, "invoke", "--interactive")
    cmd.Dir = workDir
    env := append(FilteredEnv(), "LOOM_WORKTREE_PATH="+workDir)
    if agentName != "" {
        env = append(env, "BD_ACTOR="+agentName)
    }
    cmd.Env = env

    // Pass prompt via stdin pipe (not CLI args) to avoid exposure in process listings.
    // MultiReader delivers the prompt first, then falls through to os.Stdin
    // for interactive terminal input.
    r, w, err := os.Pipe()
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to create pipe: %w", err)
    }
    if _, err := io.WriteString(w, prompt); err != nil {
        w.Close()
        r.Close()
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to write prompt to stdin: %w", err)
    }
    w.Close()
    cmd.Stdin = io.MultiReader(r, os.Stdin)

    cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
    cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr

    err = cmd.Run()
    r.Close()
    return err
}
```

Note: The `"io"` import is already present (used by `InvokeNonInteractive`).

### 2. `internal/cli/backend_external_test.go`

**Update `TestExternalBackend_InvokeInteractive` (lines 229-257):**

The current test creates a mock script that records `$@` (CLI args) and asserts the prompt appears in args. Update it to:
- Create a mock script that reads the prompt from stdin (e.g., `cat` or `read`) instead of `$@`
- Assert the prompt is received via stdin, not CLI args
- Verify the CLI args are just `invoke --interactive` (no prompt)

Updated mock script:
```sh
#!/bin/sh
echo "$@" > <argsFile>
cat > <stdinFile>
```

Updated assertions:
- Args file should contain `invoke --interactive\n` (no prompt)
- Stdin file should contain the prompt text

**Update `TestExternalBackend_EnvPassthrough` (lines 300-332):**

This test calls `InvokeInteractive` with a simple prompt. Since stdin is now piped, the mock script needs to consume stdin to avoid SIGPIPE. Add `cat > /dev/null` or similar to the mock script. The existing env assertions remain unchanged.

## Files to Create

None.

## Dependencies

None — this is a self-contained change within the external backend implementation.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Empty prompt**: `io.WriteString(w, "")` writes nothing; the pipe EOF is immediate. The external backend reads empty string from stdin, then falls through to os.Stdin. This is fine — same behavior as passing an empty CLI arg.

2. **Large prompt**: The pipe has OS-level buffering (typically 64KB on Linux, 16KB on macOS). If the prompt exceeds the pipe buffer, `io.WriteString` could block. However, since we close `w` immediately after writing, and the child process hasn't started yet (we call `cmd.Run()` after setup), the write completes before the reader starts. For very large prompts (>64KB), Go's `io.WriteString` on a pipe with no reader could block. Mitigation: write in a goroutine if needed, but in practice prompts are well under 64KB. The non-interactive path has the same pattern and works fine.

3. **Pipe creation failure**: Already handled with error return (same pattern as non-interactive path).

4. **Write failure**: Already handled with cleanup of both pipe ends and error return.

5. **Process exit before reading stdin**: The `r.Close()` after `cmd.Run()` cleans up the read end. No resource leak.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests (in `backend_external_test.go`)

1. **`TestExternalBackend_InvokeInteractive`**: Verify prompt is NOT in CLI args and IS received via stdin
2. **`TestExternalBackend_EnvPassthrough`**: Update mock script to consume stdin; verify env vars still work correctly
3. **Verify args format**: Assert the args are exactly `invoke --interactive` with no trailing prompt

### Manual Verification

1. Create a test external backend script that logs its args and stdin
2. Run `loom` with the external backend in interactive mode
3. While it's running, check `ps aux | grep loom-backend` — the prompt should NOT appear in the process listing
4. Verify the backend still receives the prompt correctly via stdin
close_reason: Completed: prompt now passed via stdin pipe instead of CLI args in InvokeInteractive, matching the non-interactive path. Tests updated to verify prompt arrives via stdin and is absent from CLI args.

title: Create container_test.go Go test harness
design:
## Summary

Create `e2e/container_test.go` — a Go test harness that orchestrates building and running the E2E Docker container from the host machine. This is the programmatic interface for the container-based E2E test suite: it builds the Docker image once via `TestMain`, then runs subtests that exercise different container configurations (full test suite, individual backends, stub overrides, error propagation). This file is what the GitHub Actions workflow (loomcli-2k9) will invoke, and it provides a Go-native entry point for developers who prefer `go test` over shell scripts.

Unlike the existing `automode_e2e_test.go` (which runs *inside* the container), `container_test.go` runs on the *host* and uses `os/exec` to invoke `docker build` and `docker run`. A separate `container` build tag prevents accidental recursion when the container runs `go test -tags e2e ./...` internally.

## Technical Approach

**Architecture: TestMain for shared build + subtests for scenarios**

The key insight is that Docker image builds are expensive (~30-60s). We build once in `TestMain` and reuse the image across all subtests. Each subtest is a separate `docker run` invocation with different flags/env vars.

**Build tag: `container`**

Using a dedicated `container` tag (not `e2e`) prevents the test from running inside the Docker container. The Dockerfile CMD uses `-tags e2e`, so `container`-tagged tests are automatically excluded. Host-side invocation uses `go test -tags container ./e2e/`.

**Key design decisions:**

1. **`TestMain` for image build**: Build the image once with `docker build -f e2e/Dockerfile -t loomcli-e2e-test .` before any tests run. If Docker is unavailable or build fails, skip all tests gracefully.

2. **Unique image tag per test run**: Use `loomcli-e2e-test-<pid>` to avoid collisions with manual `loomcli-e2e` images. Clean up via `docker rmi` in TestMain's teardown.

3. **Helper function `dockerRun`**: Wraps `docker run --rm` with context timeout, env var passthrough, and combined stdout/stderr capture. Returns exit code + output for assertions.

4. **No testcontainers dependency**: The codebase doesn't use testcontainers-go, and adding it would be over-engineering. Plain `os/exec` + `docker` CLI is sufficient and matches the project's approach (POSIX shell stubs, shell-based orchestration).

5. **Parallel subtests where safe**: Image build is serial, but `docker run` subtests can run in parallel since each container is isolated.

6. **Structured output parsing**: For tests that verify specific output (e.g., stub JSON format), parse `docker run` stdout line by line rather than using fragile regex on the full output.

## Files to Create

### 1. `e2e/container_test.go`

Go test file (~250-300 lines) with `//go:build container` tag, `package e2e_test`.

**TestMain setup/teardown:**

```
func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
    // 1. Check docker is available (exec "docker version")
    //    If not available, print skip message and os.Exit(0)
    //
    // 2. Build image with unique tag:
    //    docker build -f e2e/Dockerfile -t <imageName> .
    //    Run from repo root (detected via go.mod traversal)
    //    Timeout: 10 minutes (includes npm install, go mod download, playwright)
    //    If build fails, print output and os.Exit(1)
    //
    // 3. Run tests: code = m.Run()
    //
    // 4. Cleanup: docker rmi <imageName> (best-effort, ignore errors)
    //
    // 5. os.Exit(code)
}
```

**Helper functions:**

```
// repoRoot finds the repository root by walking up from cwd looking for go.mod
func repoRoot() (string, error)

// dockerRun executes "docker run --rm <args> <image> <cmd...>" and returns
// the combined output, exit code, and any exec error.
// Accepts a context for timeout control.
func dockerRun(ctx context.Context, env map[string]string, cmd ...string) (output string, exitCode int, err error)

// requireExitCode is a test helper that asserts the exit code matches expected.
// On mismatch, it logs the full output for debugging.
func requireExitCode(t *testing.T, expected, actual int, output string)

// assertOutputContains is a test helper that checks output contains a substring.
func assertOutputContains(t *testing.T, output, substr string)

// assertOutputNotContains is a test helper that checks output does NOT contain a substring.
func assertOutputNotContains(t *testing.T, output, substr string)
```

**Test functions:**

```
TestContainer_SmokeTest
    - Runs: docker run <image> verify_todo.sh
    - Asserts: exit code 0
    - Asserts: output contains "passed" (from verify_todo.sh summary)
    - Timeout: 2 minutes
    - Purpose: Validates container environment is correctly configured

TestContainer_FullTestSuite
    - Runs: docker run <image> run_test.sh
    - Asserts: exit code 0
    - Asserts: output contains "All phases passed"
    - Timeout: 10 minutes
    - Purpose: Runs the complete orchestrated test suite (smoke + unit + e2e)

TestContainer_BackendMatrix
    - Subtests: claude, codex, opencode
    - For each: docker run -e LOOM_BACKEND=<name> <image> run_test.sh --phase e2e --backend <name>
    - Asserts: exit code 0 for each
    - Asserts: output contains backend name in test results
    - Timeout: 5 minutes per backend
    - Purpose: Validates each backend works independently
    - Note: Can run subtests in parallel (separate containers)

TestContainer_StubExitCode
    - Runs: docker run -e STUB_CLAUDE_EXIT_CODE=1 <image> claude -p --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions
    - Asserts: exit code 1
    - Purpose: Validates stub exit code override mechanism

TestContainer_StubCustomResponse
    - Runs: docker run -e STUB_CLAUDE_RESPONSE="custom_test_response" <image> claude -p --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions
    - Asserts: output contains "custom_test_response"
    - Asserts: exit code 0
    - Purpose: Validates stub custom response mechanism

TestContainer_StubDelay
    - Runs: docker run -e STUB_CLAUDE_DELAY=2 <image> claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "hello"
    - Asserts: execution takes >= 2 seconds
    - Asserts: exit code 0
    - Timeout: 30 seconds
    - Purpose: Validates stub delay mechanism (important for timeout testing)

TestContainer_BinariesExist
    - Runs: docker run <image> sh -c "which loom && which bd && which claude && which codex && which opencode && which tmux && which git && which jq"
    - Asserts: exit code 0
    - Purpose: Quick validation that all required binaries are installed in the image

TestContainer_DefaultBackend
    - Runs: docker run <image> sh -c "echo \$LOOM_BACKEND"
    - Asserts: output contains "claude" (the default from Dockerfile ENV)
    - Purpose: Validates default environment configuration

TestContainer_ErrorPropagation
    - Runs: docker run <image> sh -c "exit 42"
    - Asserts: exit code 42
    - Purpose: Validates that container exit codes propagate to the host
      (important for CI — if tests fail inside the container, CI must detect it)
```

## Files to Modify

### 1. `e2e/Dockerfile`
No modifications needed. The existing Dockerfile copies the full source tree, so `e2e/container_test.go` will be present in the image but excluded from `go test -tags e2e ./...` because it uses the `container` build tag.

### 2. `e2e/README.md`
Add a section documenting the Go test harness:

```markdown
## Go Test Harness

Run the container tests from the host using Go's test framework:

\`\`\`bash
# Run all container tests (builds image automatically)
go test -tags container -v -timeout 15m ./e2e/

# Run a specific test
go test -tags container -v -timeout 15m -run TestContainer_SmokeTest ./e2e/

# Skip image cleanup (for debugging)
KEEP_IMAGE=1 go test -tags container -v -timeout 15m ./e2e/
\`\`\`

Note: Requires Docker to be installed and running. Tests are automatically
skipped if Docker is unavailable.
```

## Dependencies

- **Docker**: Must be installed and running on the host machine. Tests skip gracefully if Docker is unavailable.
- **e2e/Dockerfile** (loomcli-op8, completed): The Docker image definition.
- **verify_todo.sh** (loomcli-d9c, in review): Called by `TestContainer_SmokeTest`. If not yet implemented, that specific test will fail — but the harness itself can be developed independently.
- **run_test.sh** (loomcli-uqa, in review): Called by `TestContainer_FullTestSuite` and `TestContainer_BackendMatrix`. Same caveat.
- **run_local.sh** (loomcli-00s, in review): Not directly used by container_test.go. The Go harness invokes `docker build`/`docker run` directly.
- No new Go dependencies needed — only `os/exec`, `context`, `testing`, `strings`, `fmt`, `os`, `path/filepath`, `time` from stdlib.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Docker not installed**: `TestMain` checks `docker version`. If it fails, all tests are skipped with a clear message (not a failure). Use `fmt.Println("SKIP: docker not available")` + `os.Exit(0)` since `t.Skip` isn't available in `TestMain`.

2. **Docker daemon not running**: Same handling as "not installed" — `docker version` fails, tests skip.

3. **Image build failure**: If `docker build` fails in TestMain, print the full build output (for debugging), then `os.Exit(1)`. This is a hard failure, not a skip, because it likely indicates a real problem with the Dockerfile or source code.

4. **Container timeout**: Each `dockerRun` call uses `context.WithTimeout`. If a container hangs (e.g., stub with infinite delay), the context cancellation triggers `docker kill`. The test reports the timeout clearly.

5. **Exit code extraction**: When `exec.Command` runs `docker run` and the container exits non-zero, Go wraps this as an `*exec.ExitError`. The helper extracts the actual exit code from `ExitError.ExitCode()`. If the error is not an ExitError (e.g., Docker itself failed to start), treat it as exit code -1.

6. **Image cleanup failure**: If `docker rmi` fails in teardown (e.g., image in use by another container), log a warning but don't fail tests. Support `KEEP_IMAGE=1` env var to skip cleanup entirely (useful for debugging).

7. **Repo root detection**: `container_test.go` needs to run `docker build` from the repo root (so the build context includes all source files). Detect this by walking up from `os.Getwd()` looking for `go.mod`. Error if not found.

8. **Parallel test safety**: Subtests within `TestContainer_BackendMatrix` can use `t.Parallel()` safely since each runs in a separate container. However, all tests share the same image, so the image must be fully built before any subtest starts (guaranteed by TestMain).

9. **Large output handling**: Docker build output can be very large (especially npm install + go mod download). In TestMain, stream build output to stderr for real-time feedback rather than capturing it all in memory. For `docker run` in tests, capture output since it's typically small.

10. **Stale image cache**: If the Dockerfile or source code changes between test runs, the cached image may be stale. The default behavior always rebuilds (no `--cache-from`). CI can add `--no-cache` if needed.

## Testing Strategy

### Prerequisites:
- Docker installed and running
- Repository checked out at the root

### Run all container tests:
```bash
go test -tags container -v -timeout 15m ./e2e/
```

### Run individual tests:
```bash
# Just smoke test (fastest, ~1 min after build)
go test -tags container -v -timeout 5m -run TestContainer_SmokeTest ./e2e/

# Just stub tests (very fast, ~10s after build)
go test -tags container -v -timeout 5m -run TestContainer_Stub ./e2e/

# Full suite including all backends (~5 min after build)
go test -tags container -v -timeout 15m -run TestContainer_FullTestSuite ./e2e/
```

### Verify Docker-unavailable skip:
```bash
# Temporarily rename docker, run tests, verify they skip
docker_path=$(which docker) && sudo mv "$docker_path" "${docker_path}.bak"
go test -tags container -v ./e2e/ 2>&1 | grep -q "SKIP"
sudo mv "${docker_path}.bak" "$docker_path"
```

### Verify error propagation:
```bash
# The TestContainer_ErrorPropagation test covers this, but manual check:
docker build -f e2e/Dockerfile -t loomcli-e2e .
docker run loomcli-e2e sh -c "exit 42"; echo "Exit code: $?"
# Should print "Exit code: 42"
```

### Integration with CI (loomcli-2k9):
The GitHub Actions workflow will add a job that runs:
```yaml
- name: E2E Container Tests
  run: go test -tags container -v -timeout 15m ./e2e/
```

This single command handles building, running, and cleaning up — no Docker knowledge needed in the workflow file.

### Verify no recursion:
```bash
# Build and run container, verify container_test.go is NOT executed inside
docker build -f e2e/Dockerfile -t loomcli-e2e .
docker run loomcli-e2e go test -tags e2e -v -list '.*Container.*' ./e2e/ 2>&1
# Should show no matching tests (container tag not active)
```

### Manual verification checklist:
- [ ] `go test -tags container -v -timeout 15m ./e2e/` passes with Docker running
- [ ] Tests skip gracefully when Docker is not available
- [ ] Image is cleaned up after tests (unless KEEP_IMAGE=1)
- [ ] TestContainer_StubExitCode correctly detects non-zero exit
- [ ] TestContainer_StubDelay takes at least 2 seconds
- [ ] TestContainer_BackendMatrix subtests run in parallel
- [ ] Build output streams to stderr during TestMain
- [ ] No `container`-tagged tests run inside the Docker container
close_reason: Completed with code review. Created e2e/container_test.go with Go test harness, updated README.md.
